title: Whole-slide imaging and a Fiji-based image analysis workflow of immunohistochemistry staining of pancreatic islets
author: Buckels, Ross, et al.
materials: To generate the slides used for this protocol, 19 formalin-fixed ovine pancreata were paraffin-embedded, and 5 µm thick sections were cut and placed onto SuperFrost plus adhesion slides (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Five tissue sections per lamb, at least 100 µm apart, underwent multiplexed immunohistochemistry (IHC) for insulin, glucagon, and somatostatin [9]. A detailed description of this methodology can be found in Supplementary Method Note 1.
The image is cropped according to 2.2 above.2.3.

steps.title: Prepare paraffin slides
steps.instruction: Fix 19 ovine pancreata in formalin, embed them in paraffin, cut 5 µm thick sections, and mount each section onto SuperFrost plus adhesion slides (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Place five sections per lamb at least 100 µm apart and perform multiplexed immunohistochemistry for insulin, glucagon, and somatostatin as described in Supplementary Method Note 1.

steps.title: Acquire images and name files
steps.instruction: Scan each slide with the MetaSystems VSlide slide‑scanner (or equivalent) and save files using the naming hierarchy required by the protocol. The hierarchy is: user initials followed by an underscore, date of acquisition (YYMMDD), four‑letter project code “Sild”, protocol ID “IGS” (insulin, glucagon, somatostatin), slide run number (10‑90), and a six‑digit animal ID (e.g., EB_160117_Sild_IGS_10_XXXXXX). During acquisition a six‑digit FOV ID (e.g., Img‑000001) and a classifier suffix (B for DAPI, Y for insulin, G for glucagon, O for somatostatin) are appended. Save files according to the hierarchy shown in Table 1; macro 01 will later append the correct slide number and animal ID to each FOV ID. Perform image acquisition on individual FOV images because whole‑slide files often exceed 2 GB, which would otherwise require high‑performance computers.

steps.title: Configure Fiji environment
steps.instruction: Install the same version of Fiji used in the study, place all ImageJ1Macro (.ijm) files in the Fiji macros folder, and verify that the file extension used by the classifier files matches the expectation of macro “02 Analysis macro.ijm”. If the extension differs, edit lines 93, 97, 101, and 105 of the macro accordingly.

steps.title: Crop and rename images
steps.instruction: Open Fiji macro “01 Cropping and renaming macro.ijm”, confirm the region of interest for cropping at line 72 (based on overlap between neighboring FOVs), and run the macro. The macro creates a duplicate of each original image, crops it according to the confirmed ROI, creates a new folder for each slideID with the suffix “Crop”, renames each cropped image, and saves it in the new folder.

steps.title: Set calibration and thresholds
steps.instruction: Open macro “02 Analysis macro.ijm”. Confirm the system calibration at line 116 (3.1 pixels µm⁻¹ for the objective lens and camera). Confirm the background‑tissue threshold at line 170 and the positive‑staining thresholds at line 200 (insulin), line 226 (glucagon), and line 253 (somatostatin). Adjust these values as needed for the specific staining batch.

steps.title: Run analysis macro
steps.instruction: Run macro “02 Analysis macro.ijm”. The macro (a) defines regions with no pancreatic tissue by pseudo‑colouring the four channel images, merging them, converting to binary, overlaying the binary mask on the composite, and saving the result; (b) opens each cropped channel image (insulin, glucagon, somatostatin), applies the user‑specified threshold, converts to binary, measures regions larger than a user‑defined size threshold to exclude debris, overlays the measured regions on the binary image, and saves the overlays; (c) creates an “outputs” folder within each slideID that contains seven images per FOV and a summary text file with quantitative measurements.

Create ‘outputs’ folder with images and summary file

steps.title: Perform image quality control
steps.instruction: For each slide, compare the output images from approximately 10 FOVs to the raw fluorophore images to verify that the chosen thresholds produce accurate segmentation; if not, adjust thresholds and rerun the analysis. Then examine the whole‑section stitched images in MetaViewer (or equivalent) to identify artefacts such as tissue folding, focus problems, or excessive background staining, and exclude any FOVs with artefacts from further analysis.

Adjust thresholds and repeat analysis if needed

steps.title: Pool and summarize results
steps.instruction: Use Power Query in Microsoft Excel to import all summary text files into a single table. Remove rows corresponding to excluded FOVs. With Power Pivot, calculate for each slideID the sum of background area, total image area, insulin‑positive area, glucagon‑positive area, and somatostatin‑positive area. Then, using Power Pivot, calculate for each animal ID the average of those summed values. Report the final table with measurements in µm².
